title: Israeli strike hits air defence radar site near Isfahan in Iran
body:
On 19 April 2024 at about 05:23 Iran Standard Time, Israel carried out a limited strike near Isfahan in central Iran, in response to Iran's drone and missile attack of 13 and 14 April. The target was an air defence radar site at an airbase near the city. A US official told ABC News that Israeli aircraft, operating beyond Iran's borders, fired three missiles at a radar site guarding the Natanz nuclear facility.

Accounts of the damage differed. According to the US account, the radar site was destroyed, while satellite imagery indicated an S-300 radar in the Isfahan area was damaged or destroyed, with no extensive damage to the airbase itself. Iranian officials said there was no damage or casualties and that air defences shot down three drones over Isfahan. An Iranian official told Reuters the explosions came from Israeli drones being downed and that there was no missile attack. The International Atomic Energy Agency confirmed that no damage occurred to Iran's nuclear sites.

A senior US official said Israel had notified the US in advance and that the strike was meant to show Israel's capabilities without escalating tensions. The Israeli military had no comment at the time, and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir called the attack "feeble." Israeli minister Miri Regev confirmed Israeli responsibility on 5 May 2024. Syrian radar positions were also reportedly hit in related strikes. The exchange was the first in which Israel and Iran struck each other's territory directly, and the next Israeli strikes on Iran came on 26 October 2024.
